thread:
jasmin: Heads-up — seeing a p95 spike after we rolled the KV-aware admission heuristic to prod. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/r/queues, p95 small-seq jumped ~220ms -> ~380ms in the last 2h.

mike: Saw it. Same trend on our side. p50 stable, p95 and p99 increased. Looks like increased queue wait rather than decode. @sara any config changes landed with that patch?

sara: We flipped on KV-aware grouping and bumped token_budget_target to 48 for the continuous-batcher experiment. Also enabled dynamic kernel toggles (suggest kernel per-request based on kv_shape). Config snippet I deployed: 
```
batch_policy:\n  token_target: 48\n  kv_aware: true\n  soft_limit: 10\n  allow_kernel_suggestions: true\n```

kevin: Do we have telemetry breaking down wait_time by kv_hit vs kv_miss? Intuition: kv_hits should reduce decode time but can increase admission delay because we try to group same-kv keys to improve kv-cache reuse.

infra-bot: Rollout event: admit-service v2.3 deployed to prod at 2026-02-15T03:12:45Z (canary=10%).

jasmin: I profiled a canary node: there's a hot path where admission consults kv-shape and then calls kernel_selector for each request. We're seeing lots of `kernel_suggestion=dynamic` churn. Example log: 
`[03:20:12] admit: req=0x7f3e kv_hit=true kv_shape=(1,128) kernel_suggestion=dynamic wait_ms=42`

mike: That per-request kernel decision likely serializes batch formation. If kernel selection is expensive we need to unify it at batch formation time — compute a single kernel for the batch instead of per-request. Also, we should avoid delaying admission trying to get ideal kv-cohort size.

sara: Another complicating factor: token_budget_target=48 increases how long we wait for enough tokens for a batch. For short sequences that adds obvious extra wait. We tried to tune to improve throughput / cost but it hurts tail latency.

kevin: Two proposal threads: (1) Roll back the KV-aware admission to stop the regression quickly. (2) Longer-term: implement KV-aware accounting but make it non-blocking — prefer grouping but not at the cost of exceeding soft_limit. Also instrument per-priority token credits so high-priority traffic doesn't get queued behind cohort formation.

mike: +1. For (2) we can add a soft-reject that returns 429 with an estimated backoff header instead of letting requests pile up. Example: `Retry-After: 0.3` and `X-Estimated-WaitMs: 320`. Clients can choose to retry or fall back.

sara: We previously tried 429 soft-reject and saw retry storms from naive clients. Alternative: degraded fallback — when queue depth > soft_limit route to a cheaper model variant (lower memory/quantized) with a per-route opt-out flag. That avoids client retry loops and keeps success rate high.

kevin: If we route to degraded variant we must account for deterministic/contract customers. Add `allow_fallback: true|false` per route. Also, record kv_hit-adjusted token charge: kv_hits cost fewer decode tokens, so admission should charge less to preserve fairness — e.g. charge 0.6x tokens for kv_hit in the budget pool.

jasmin: Action plan I propose:
1) Roll back KV-aware admission in prod immediately to stabilize p95.
2) Ship a patch that removes per-request kernel_selection and instead selects kernel at batch formation (cheap heuristic: choose kernel by majority kv_shape or by max_seq_len in batch).
3) Add per-route token credits + kv_hit discount to admission accounting.
4) Emit new telemetry: wait_time_by_kv_hit, kernel_switch_count, batch_formation_time.
5) Re-run synthetic perf tests with controlled KV-hit ratios before re-enabling.
Can we get (1)-(3) out as hotfix today?

mike: I'll open PR for the kernel-selection change and the hotfix. Will target canary=5% and add extra tracing.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-4721 - transient p95 regression in runtime queues (assigned: eng-runtime, priority: P2).

sara: I'll prepare a perf harness: synthetic load with 70% kv-hit, seq mix [20, 128, 512], and measure batch sizes, kernel flips, and queue wait. Also prepare a client-side guidance doc about Retry-After handling.

kevin: Also, a thought for future: admission could compute an optimistic kernel offline using cached shapes and only do full kernel selection if batch composition changes. That might give us most benefits with minimal latency overhead.

jasmin: Great. Thanks — please ping this thread when PR is up. I'll notify #eng-runtime and on-call if p99 goes above 700ms.

mike: PR link when ready — tagging @sara @kevin for reviews. :thumbsup:
